The PKGBUILD file defines a standard binary package build process for `vodarr-bin`, sourcing pre-built binaries from the project's official GitHub releases page. The package installs only two files: the binary to `/usr/bin/vodarr` with appropriate permissions, and the license file to the standard location under `/usr/share/licenses`. No scripts are executed during the build or install phase beyond these direct file placements. While the package depends on common system tools (ca-certificates and ffmpeg), this is expected given its purpose of downloading and processing media content. The source URLs point exclusively to the declared upstream repository (github.com/combor/vodarr), and no network activity or external fetches are performed during build time. Overall, the PKGBUILD follows secure and conventional practices for distributing a signed, versioned binary.
</details>

All sources point to official GitHub releases under the `combor/vodarr` repository, which aligns with the declared upstream URL. The package downloads prebuilt binaries from the GitHub release page, which is common for `-bin` packages in the AUR. While distributing precompiled binaries carries inherent trust assumptions (users must trust the maintainer and the release integrity), this practice is not inherently malicious and falls within standard AUR packaging norms. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, runtime downloads, or unauthorized network activity in the metadata. The dependencies and conflicts are appropriate for the described application functionality.

No evidence of malicious behavior, such as unauthorized data exfiltration, dynamic code fetching, or execution of unverified payloads, is present in this file. The content strictly adheres to expected AUR metadata conventions.
